Skip next section Russian authorities report more deaths in Ukrainian attacks 09/07/2026 September 7, 2026 Russian authorities report more deaths in Ukrainian attacks Russian authorities have reported further deaths from Ukrainian attacks, including two people killed in Russian-annexed Crimea, as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed strikes on targets deep inside Russia. The latest reports expand on earlier accounts of deadly drone attacks in Russia's Perm and Belgorod regions. In Sevastopol, the Moscow-appointed governor, Mikhail Razvozhayev, said a man and a teenage girl were killed in a Ukrainian attack. Eight apartment buildings were also damaged, he said. Russia annexed Crimea from Ukraine in 2014. Kyiv has repeatedly targeted the peninsula, which Russia uses as a military staging and supply base. Zelenskyy confirmed that Ukrainian forces had attacked a number of targets in Russia. He said a refinery in the Ryazan region had been damaged, while refineries in the Perm region and the Republic of Tatarstan had also been targeted. Zelenskyy said Ukrainian forces had additionally struck targets in the Kursk region and the Black Sea. https://p.dw.com/p/5M6CV Skip next section UN rights chief urges ban on fully autonomous weapons 09/07/2026 September 7, 2026 UN rights chief urges ban on fully autonomous weapons Wesley Dockery Editor The UN human rights chief has called for an urgent ban on weapons that can kill without human involvement, citing reports that fully autonomous drones have already caused deaths in Ukraine. Volker Türk said he was "horrified" by reports that Russian forces used a fully autonomous drone to kill three Ukrainians last month, while also noting reports that Ukraine had field-tested similar systems. The New York Times reported last month that a Russian drone guided entirely by artificial intelligence killed three civilians in Zaporizhzhia in southeastern Ukraine on July 6. According to the report, human operators had programmed the drone to travel toward a particular petrol station, but the system itself selected the precise target, thought to have been propane tanks. Türk, the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, also highlighted reports that Ukraine had tested autonomous weapons. There has been growing pressure from international organizations and NGOs to regulate so-called lethal autonomous weapons , sometimes referred to as "killer robots." "I join calls for the urgent prohibition of weapons that can take lives without human involvement," Türk told the UN Human Rights Council. After years of debate, 128 countries agreed at the UN on Saturday on a definition of autonomous weapons. NGOs have accused the United States and Russia in particular of trying to weaken the agreed language. AI on the march—a new age of killer robots? The revelation adds to the significance of one of the most high-profile Russian strikes on a Ukrainian government building since the start of the full-scale invasion. SBU chief Oleksandr Poklad was not there at the time and was unharmed. Zelenskyy said he had instructed the SBU to prepare an "appropriate, tangible response" and suggested Ukraine could retaliate in a similar manner. Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called the strike a "major escalation." Black smoke was seen rising from the SBU building, close to the UNESCO-listed St. Sophia Cathedral. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said at least 12 people were wounded in the wider attack on the capital, although it was not immediately clear whether any of them were injured at the SBU headquarters. The strike also damaged nearby buildings and shattered windows in the area. It was the first time the SBU headquarters had been hit since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022. The SBU plays a central role in Ukraine's war effort and has carried out long-range and covert operations against Russian military targets. It was behind Operation Spiderweb in 2025, when drones targeted Russian strategic bombers at air bases deep inside Russia, as well as the 2022 bombing of the bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea. One person was killed and four others were injured in Russia's Perm region after a drone attack damaged a residential building, regional Governor Dmitry Makhonin said. He said local air defense units had shot down 27 Ukranian drones over the region, which lies deep inside Russia. In the Belgorod region, which borders Ukraine , one person was killed and another injured in a separate Ukrainian drone attack, according to local authorities. The talks produced upbeat assessments from both sides but no announced breakthrough in efforts to end the war. "We very much hope that we will be able to reach agreements with our American partners, and we are counting on the support of our European partners if the war continues in winter — and this is how it appears at the moment," Zelenskyy said. He also said Ukraine would hold talks with the US, France and Germany, without giving further details. Zelenskyy again argued that the most difficult territorial issues could only be resolved in a meeting between leaders. US envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner , US President Donald Trump's son-in-law, had traveled to Kyiv a day after meeting Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow. Putin had announced a three-day pause in attacks on Kyiv for the duration of the US negotiators' visit. Ukraine, in turn, refrained from attacking Moscow during the same period. Zelenskyy joked that the presence of Witkoff and Kushner had "worked better than the Patriot air defense systems." It was Witkoff and Kushner’s first visit to the Ukrainian capital, a repeated target of Russian strikes since the start of Moscow's full-scale invasion. The pair have made several visits to Moscow. While Witkoff and Zelenskyy both described Sunday's talks positively, neither side announced a concrete breakthrough. https://p.dw.com/p/5M3AY Skip next section Welcome to our coverage 09/07/2026 September 7, 2026 Welcome to our coverage Richard Connor | Elizabeth Schumacher Editor You join us after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy downplayed hopes of a quick end to the conflict, saying the fighting currently appears likely to continue into winter. https://www.euronews.com/2026/09/24/us-p.text: In a grand welcome, US President Donald Trump greeted his Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping, on the tarmac of Joint Base Andrews, just outside of Washington, D.C, on Wednesday, for his three-day state visit, as their top officials agreed to prolong a trade truce until January.The truce, which includes both countries agreeing to scale back tariffs and not impose new trade restrictions, was announced by Trump's Treasury Secretary, Bessent, during a Fox News Channel interview, “I don’t know whether a bigger deal can be done. I don’t know whether we will just roll the current deal,” Bessent said.However, upcoming international summits in China in November and Florida in December could give the two sides new opportunities to discuss the matter, the Treasury Secretary added.Xi says China and the US 'should be partners not rivals'In a statement upon Xi's arrival in the US, accompanied by his wife, Peng Liyuan, the leader wrote that his country and the US “should be partners, not rivals. Achieving the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and making America great again can go hand in hand and the two countries can contribute to each other’s success, thereby benefiting the wider world.”In comments released by Chinese state media Xi also said that he was looking "forward to in-depth exchanges with President Trump on major issues concerning our bilateral relations and the global situation,".Trade alongside artificial intelligence, Trump's war with Iran and China's position on Taiwan have been among the biggest issues between the two superpowers, but this visit is expected to be more about show than substance.Backlash among republicansMeanwhile Xi's welcoming has caused backlash among some of the Republicans, Sen. Roger Wicker, chairman of the Senate Armed Services Committee, criticised the “lavish welcome.” saying during a speech on Tuesday in the Senate that Trump should not have invited the Chinese leader “based on all of the troubling issues we have with President Xi and the Chinese Communist Party.”As Secretary of State, Marco Rubio said that the US and China need to maintain their relationship at the highest level since the countries are "the two largest economies in the world” and “probably the two most powerful militaries in the world.”Xi's first state visit to the US in more than a decade is expected to be marked by a formal welcome banquet, another flyover, talks in the Oval Office and a state banquet at the White House on Thursday.Before wrapping up on Friday after tea at the White House and a visit to the National Archives, home the US Declaration of Independance.
